archetype: Golgari reanimator: load a fat creature, return it on turn three or four, and let Meren return it again each end step, with Grave Pact and Dictate of Erebos turning deaths into edicts. The declared goldfish frame (death drain) no longer matches this list, and the audit applied base targets because no archetype was established.
verdict: It is fast and deep. Mana is reliable (0.91 turn-3 land drop), there are 10 tutors, and 11 of its 19 interaction pieces are on creatures Meren can return. It also has six answers to a Rest in Peace or Leyline of the Void. What limits it at a real table is that nothing in the 99 stops a counterspell on the reanimate turn, and that its card flow depends on its own graveyard: Meren returns a creature card every end step and five of its seven draw cards need a death, an entry or attack, or combat damage, so a wipe followed by graveyard exile is the hand it cannot rebuild from.

components.reading: The loaders: five tutor directly to the graveyard, the rest discard or mill. Deep enough; the stale declaration does not measure them.

Seven reanimation effects plus Meren. Four of them (Persist, Victimize, Agadeem's Awakening, Sheoldred) and Meren read only our graveyard. Animate Dead, Reanimate and Necromancy can take from any graveyard; Tergrid (an opponent's sacrificed or discarded permanent card) and The True Scriptures' chapter III (gated) also take from opponents' yards. Persist and Unmarked Grave cannot touch the legendary targets (Hogaak, both Sheoldreds, Tergrid).

components.reading: The fat. Only four are nonlegendary (Archon, Craterhoof, Grave Titan, Noxious Gearhulk), so only those four work with Unmarked Grave and Persist.

Ten sacrifice outlets that cost no mana (Phyrexian Tower and High Market once per turn). The stale declaration names five of them and reads 68.6% for those five; the full set is unmeasured and higher. This component can give up a slot.
Six recurring token makers (counting Scute Swarm) plus two one-shot bodies. Enough fodder for Skullclamp and for the outlets.
Read by the text, this is the thinnest component. None of the four stops a counterspell. Spore Frog stops only combat damage, and Malakir Rebirth covers one creature against one death.

single_points_of_failure.why: Persist, Victimize, Agadeem's Awakening, Sheoldred's upkeep return, Meren's return, Hogaak's cast from the graveyard, Woe Strider's escape and Takenuma's channel all read only our yard; Animate Dead, Reanimate and Necromancy fall back on an opponent's. A Rest in Peace or Leyline of the Void can be answered: Assassin's Trophy, Beast Within, Cankerbloom, Haywire Mite, Boseiju and Glissa all remove an enchantment. No card in the 99 stops an instant-speed exile (Bojuka Bog, a Soul-Guide Lantern activation). Takenuma, Abandoned Mire's channel ({3}{B}, from hand, whenever we have priority) answers it in part: in response it returns one creature card to hand before the exile resolves. Whether Necromancy in response saves a second target, to the battlefield, is an open question. After one, the recovery is hard-casting from hand, Meren's end-step return needs a creature card in our yard, and five of the seven draw cards need a death, an entry or attack, or combat damage.

Goldfish defect: goldfish_profiles.draw_profile reads Veil of Summer's conditional draw ('Draw a card if an opponent has cast a blue or black spell this turn') as spell_draw 1, an unconditional cantrip. findings.note: Round-2 over-claim fixed. The Takenuma oracle text in the corpus reads 'Channel — {3}{B}, Discard this card: Mill three cards, then return a creature or planeswalker card from your graveyard to your hand.' It is an activated ability from hand, usable at instant speed, so it resolves before Bojuka Bog's ETB trigger (which targets a player) or a Soul-Guide Lantern activation. 'Answers it in part ... returns one creature card to hand' is accurate. I enumerated every card in cards.json whose oracle text mentions a graveyard and that is an instant, has flash or channel: Entomb, Necromancy, Takenuma and Agadeem (a sorcery). So Takenuma and Necromancy are the only candidates, and the re-scoped superlative holds. Minor point: the base cost is quoted, but with Meren in play the legendary discount makes it {2}{B}. That understates the answer and does not make it false. The Necromancy clause here shares the defect recorded on open_questions[1].

'If Necromancy also works, it is the second partial answer and the only one that puts the creature onto the battlefield.' Necromancy's own oracle text reads 'If you cast it any time a sorcery couldn't have been cast, the controller of the permanent it becomes sacrifices it at the beginning of the next cleanup step.' Cast in response to Bog or Lantern, which is by definition not sorcery timing, the creature stays only until cleanup. You get its ETB and a possible block, and it then goes back to a yard that has already been exiled, so it is still around for a later reanimation. That is real value, but it is not 'onto the battlefield' as a lasting answer, and the rider is never mentioned. The matching clause in engine.single_points_of_failure[0] ('saves a second target, to the battlefield') inherits the same omission. The timing question itself is answered by the printed flash permission. What a resolve-stack would actually settle is what the cleanup sacrifice leaves behind. I accepted this framing in round 2 ('Necromancy returns to the battlefield rather than to hand'); that was my miss, and this note corrects it. Fix: state the cleanup sacrifice and re-scope the claim to 'a one-turn body plus the card back in the post-exile yard'.

Re-ran `try meren-recursion --out "Elvish Mystic" --in "Veil of Summer"` (10,000 games per list). Every figure reproduces: 3 better, 5 worse, 7 no call. Worse: damage @T10 24.4->23.7 [-1.1,-0.3], 6+ drop by T6 30.0->29.5 [-0.9,-0.3], killed by T6 4.4->4.2 [-0.3,-0.1], board power -0.09 [-0.12,-0.06], experience -0.07 [-0.09,-0.05]. Better: missed drop 43.7->42.7 [-1.1,-0.8], extra cards 1.74->1.86 [+0.11,+0.13], turns saved 1.91->1.99 [+0.06,+0.09]. Sources: G +8 -> +7, B -2 unchanged. The better side is now quoted. The artefact claim holds: corpus oracle 'Draw a card if an opponent has cast a blue or black spell this turn'. The pool card carries no oracle key, so I fed draw_profile a dict with oracle_text set, and it returns spell_draw 1. 'Plausibly ride on that phantom card' on the missed-drop and big-body rows is hedged as the screen cannot separate it, which is right. And 'the real cost is at least the five worse rows' points the right way, because the phantom draw props up the branch.

The new goldfish-defect entry matches what I reproduced: draw_profile on Veil of Summer's oracle_text gives spell_draw 1, while the printed draw is conditional on an opponent's blue or black spell, which a goldfish never casts. 'Fix the conditional-cantrip parse, then re-screen' is the right remedy.
